---
title: "Getting started in ten minutes"
pareja: lupa.Rmd

::: {lang="en"}

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(lupa)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
# The width is restored at the end, as the CRAN Cookbook asks.
.opciones_previas <- options(width = 90)

# Printing a profile reports the memory the table takes. That figure changes
# with the platform and the R version, and a guide does not publish memory
# sizes: chunks marked with `sin_memoria = TRUE` drop that line.
.quitar_memoria <- function(gancho) {
  force(gancho)
  function(x, options) {
    if (isTRUE(options$sin_memoria)) {
      lineas <- strsplit(x, "\n", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
      lineas <- lineas[!grepl("Memoria: ", lineas, fixed = TRUE)]
      # Each line of the general summary arrives as its own message: if the
      # memory line was the only one, nothing is left to show.
      if (!length(lineas)) return("")
      x <- paste0(paste(lineas, collapse = "\n"), "\n")
    }
    gancho(x, options)
  }
}
knitr::knit_hooks$set(
  message = .quitar_memoria(knitr::knit_hooks$get("message")),
  output = .quitar_memoria(knitr::knit_hooks$get("output"))
)
```

> This guide is the English version of
> [1. Empezar en diez minutos](lupa.html). `lupa` writes its messages and tables
> in Spanish, so the output below is in Spanish.

A table arrives and, before using it, we want to know whether we can trust it.
What is wrong with it, in which rows are the problems, and what could not be
checked?

> **In this guide:**
>
> - we profile a table with `perfilar()` and read its summary;
> - we start with the findings of severity `error`;
> - we go from a finding to the rows of the source system with `clave`;
> - we read in `cobertura()` what could not be evaluated;
> - we save a report and clean a column in a copy.

## The data

`datos_operativos` (operational data) comes with the package:
`r nrow(lupa::datos_operativos)` synthetic records from an event system, with
defects planted on purpose. Before profiling, we look at them.

```{r datos}
library(lupa)
datos_operativos
```

This is what each column carries (`?datos_operativos` describes it), with the
finding that flags it:

| column | what it carries on purpose | finding that flags it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id_registro` | `1` and `10` repeated; the 2 rows with `10` differ in the rest | `posible_identificador` (possible identifier); the repetition, once declared as a key (guide 2) |
| `codigo_usuario` | `"S/D"` instead of a missing value; `USR0003` and `MAL-5` outside the format | `faltantes_disfrazados` (disguised missing values); the formats, none (see below why) |
| `fecha_evento` | 5 date formats and a `"NULL"` | `formatos_fecha_mixtos` (mixed date formats), `faltantes_disfrazados` |
| `canal` | `"web"`, `"Web"` and `"web "`; `"S/D"` and an empty cell | `mayusculas_inconsistentes` (inconsistent capitalization), `espacios_sobrantes` (extra spaces), `faltantes_disfrazados` |
| `monto` | `-99`, `0`, `-50` and `999999` | `faltantes_disfrazados` for the `-99`; the `0` and the `-50`, only if we declare that they are not allowed (`columnas_sin_ceros`, `columnas_no_negativas`: columns without zeros, non-negative columns); the `999999`, none (see below why) |
| `sistema` | the same value in every row | `constante` (constant) |
| `contacto` | synthetic emails and one malformed | `dato_personal_posible` (possible personal data); the malformed one, none (for the same reason as the formats of `codigo_usuario`) |
| `id_copia` | a copy of `id_registro` | `columnas_duplicadas` (duplicated columns) |
| `id_evento` | the identifier of the event; `EVT001` twice | `clave_no_unica` (non-unique key), once declared as a key |
| rows 1 and 12 | identical | `filas_duplicadas` (duplicated rows) |

`zona` carries no defects.

## Profiling

`perfilar()` (*profile*) reads the table without modifying it. In `clave`
(*key*) we pass the column that identifies each event in the source system. That
way, where a finding points to rows, it says which events they are.

```{r perfilar}
perfil <- perfilar(datos_operativos, clave = "id_evento")
```

The warning is the first result: the key we declared repeats. `lupa` does not
take it for granted; it checks it. Printing the profile shows the summary:

```{r imprimir, sin_memoria = TRUE}
perfil
```

The first 4 lines count the findings by severity and the diagnostics that could
not be evaluated:

- `error`: a check crossed its criterion;
- `sospechoso` (*suspicious*): something deserves a look;
- `ok`: an informative reading, not a defect.

Below come the general summary and a few measures per column. The printout also
shows the memory the table takes; we leave it out here because it changes with
the R installation.

## Starting with the errors

The findings that `hallazgos()` (*findings*) returns are a table, and they are
filtered like any `data.frame`.

```{r errores}
h <- hallazgos(perfil)
h[h$severidad == "error", c("columna", "tipo_hallazgo", "n_afectados")]
```

```{r cifras-errores, include = FALSE}
errores <- h[h$severidad == "error", ]
n_errores <- nrow(errores)
de_tabla <- errores$tipo_hallazgo[is.na(errores$columna)]
```

There are `r n_errores`. A `columna` (*column*) in `NA` marks a finding about
the whole table. Rows 1 and 12 are identical
(`filas_duplicadas`), and that is why `EVT001` appears twice in the key
(`clave_no_unica`).

```{r comprobar-errores, echo = FALSE}
# The table of planted defects promises these findings.
prometidos <- list(
  c("id_registro", "posible_identificador"), c("codigo_usuario", "faltantes_disfrazados"),
  c("fecha_evento", "formatos_fecha_mixtos"), c("fecha_evento", "faltantes_disfrazados"),
  c("canal", "mayusculas_inconsistentes"), c("canal", "espacios_sobrantes"),
  c("canal", "faltantes_disfrazados"), c("monto", "faltantes_disfrazados"),
  c("sistema", "constante"), c("contacto", "dato_personal_posible")
)
for (par in prometidos) {
  stopifnot(any(h$columna %in% par[1] & h$tipo_hallazgo == par[2]))
}
stopifnot(
  "columnas_duplicadas" %in% h$tipo_hallazgo,
  !any(h$columna %in% "zona"),
  setequal(de_tabla, c("clave_no_unica", "filas_duplicadas")),
  all(c("faltantes_disfrazados", "formatos_fecha_mixtos") %in% errores$tipo_hallazgo)
)
```

## From the finding to the row

We take one: the disguised missing values of `canal` (*channel*). The
`evidencia` (evidence) says what was seen; the `sugerencia` (suggestion), what
could be done.

```{r un-hallazgo}
canal <- h[h$columna %in% "canal" & h$tipo_hallazgo == "faltantes_disfrazados", ]
writeLines(canal$evidencia)
writeLines(strwrap(canal$sugerencia, 88))
```

The `trazabilidad` (traceability) says in which rows it is, with the values of
the key we declared.

```{r traza}
eventos <- canal$trazabilidad[[1]]$claves$id_evento
eventos
```

With those identifiers we look up the events in the source system, without
opening the whole table. Here we can check them (with quotes, so that the empty
cell shows):

```{r cotejo}
filas <- datos_operativos$id_evento %in% eventos
print(datos_operativos[filas, c("id_evento", "canal")], quote = TRUE)
```

```{r comprobar-traza, echo = FALSE}
stopifnot(identical(eventos, c("EVT005", "EVT011")))
```

Without `clave`, the traceability carries only the row numbers, which work
inside R but not in the source system.

## ⚠️ What could not be evaluated {#what-could-not-be-evaluated}

A check that found nothing is not the same as a check that did not run. The
second case stays in `cobertura()` (*coverage*), with the reason and how to
solve it.

```{r cobertura}
no_evaluados <- cobertura(perfil)
no_evaluados[, c("diagnostico", "columna")]
```

The `999999` of `monto` (*amount*) is not among the findings, and not because it
is fine. The search for extreme values did not run on that column:

```{r motivo}
motivo <- no_evaluados$motivo[
  no_evaluados$diagnostico == "outliers" & no_evaluados$columna == "monto"
]
writeLines(strwrap(motivo, 88))
```

What could not be measured stays on record; it never counts as zero.

The odd formats of `codigo_usuario` (`USR0003` and `MAL-5`) have no finding
either, for another reason: that check did run. Each format takes 1 row out of
`r nrow(datos_operativos)`. By default, a format is rare when it stays below
`r 100 * formals(perfilar)$umbral_patron_raro`% of the values
(`umbral_patron_raro`, the rare-pattern threshold). In a longer table it would
be flagged.

```{r comprobar-cobertura, echo = FALSE}
stopifnot(
  length(motivo) == 1L,
  !any(h$columna %in% "monto" & h$tipo_hallazgo == "outliers"),
  !any(h$columna %in% c("codigo_usuario", "contacto") & h$tipo_hallazgo == "patron_raro"),
  !any(h$tipo_hallazgo %in% c("ceros_no_permitidos", "negativos_no_permitidos")),
  1 / nrow(datos_operativos) > formals(perfilar)$umbral_patron_raro
)
```

## 📄 A report to share {#a-report-to-share}

`reportar()` (*report*) writes a single HTML file. It opens in any browser and
needs no network and no other programs.

```{r informe}
archivo <- file.path(tempdir(), "calidad-de-la-entrega.html")
reportar(perfil, archivo = archivo, titulo = "Calidad de la entrega")
```

```{r secciones, include = FALSE}
html <- paste(readLines(archivo, encoding = "UTF-8", warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n")
secciones <- regmatches(html, gregexpr("<h3[^>]*>.*?</h3>", html, perl = TRUE))[[1]]
secciones <- gsub("<[^>]+>", "", secciones)
stopifnot(length(secciones) > 0L)
```

The report has these sections: `r paste(secciones, collapse = "; ")`.
`reportar()` returns the path of the file; in an interactive session,
`browseURL(archivo)` opens it in the browser. It also accepts the full result of
`analizar()`, with the measurements and the cleaning plan: we see it in
[3. Explorar columnas con `analizar()`](explorar-columnas.html)
(*Exploring columns with `analizar()`*, in Spanish).

## Cleaning a column

`lupa` does not change the data it profiles. To clean, it proposes an editable
plan; `aplicar()` (*apply*) runs on a copy only the actions we mark.

```{r plan}
plan <- planificar_limpieza(perfil, datos_operativos)
plan[plan$columna %in% "canal", c("id_accion", "estrategia", "recomendada", "aplicar")]
```

For `canal`, the plan recommends and leaves marked
`r sum(plan$columna %in% "canal" & plan$recomendada)` actions:

- turning into `NA` the missing values written as text;
- trimming the spaces at the edges.

Between lower case, upper case or a dictionary it does not choose: that decision
is ours. Each action carries its justification, which also says what is worth
confirming:

```{r justificacion}
justificacion <- plan$justificacion[
  plan$columna %in% "canal" & plan$estrategia == "convertir_ausencias_textuales"
]
writeLines(strwrap(justificacion, 88))
```

For this guide we apply only those
`r sum(plan$columna %in% "canal" & plan$recomendada)` actions.

```{r aplicar}
plan$aplicar <- plan$columna %in% "canal" & plan$recomendada
limpio <- aplicar(plan, datos_operativos)
limpio$registro[, c("columna", "estrategia", "n_cambiadas", "estado")]
```

We compare the values before and after in the rows that changed:

```{r antes-despues}
antes <- datos_operativos$canal
despues <- limpio$datos$canal
cambiaron <- is.na(despues) | antes != despues
print(data.frame(id_evento = datos_operativos$id_evento, antes, despues)[cambiaron, ],
      quote = TRUE)
```

The `antes` (before) column was read from `datos_operativos` after applying the
plan: the original stays as it was. `"Web"` and `"APP"` stayed the same, because
we did not choose any capitalization convention. The full plan, with its groups
of actions and its log, is in
[6. Limpiar con un plan](limpiar-con-un-plan.html) (*Cleaning with a plan*, in
Spanish).

```{r comprobar-limpieza, echo = FALSE}
stopifnot(
  identical(sum(cambiaron), 3L),
  identical(antes[cambiaron], c("S/D", "web ", "")),
  identical(despues[!is.na(despues) & cambiaron], "web")
)
```

## Summary

- `perfilar()` reads the table without modifying it; its printout counts the
  findings by severity and what could not be evaluated.
- `hallazgos()` is a table: we start with `severidad == "error"`.
- With `clave`, the traceability of each finding carries the identifiers to go
  to the source system.
- `cobertura()` lists the checks that did not run: a missing finding does not
  prove that the data is fine.
- `reportar()` saves an HTML report; `planificar_limpieza()` (*plan the
  cleaning*) and `aplicar()` clean a copy with the actions we choose.
